conviction_note: I anchor magnitude on the 9.27% historical median, not the 24.46% option print — 297 total OI and a 67%-of-mid ATM spread is a quote, not a market, and 48.8% annualised 20d realised vol (~3.1%/day) independently implies an earnings day near 9-10%, so the chain is the outlier; within that envelope the signed tilt is modestly positive, carried almost entirely by a one-sided tax tail that the -22.5% run-up cannot be discounting.

findings.finding: RF Industries added brand-new deferred-tax-asset release language to its Q2 FY2026 10-Q MD&A that is absent from the Q1 10-Q filed three months earlier — 'it is reasonably possible that a reduction of a significant portion of the valuation allowance may be appropriate in a future reporting period', with 'cumulative losses' recast into the past tense ('In prior periods, the Company recorded a valuation allowance due primarily to cumulative losses') — against a $4,521,000 allowance which on 11,424,572 diluted shares is roughly $0.40 per share of potential one-time GAAP EPS, versus a $0.18 two-analyst consensus.
findings.why_not_priced: This lives in the MD&A of a $110m microcap's 10-Q, not in the release, not in the 8-K exhibit and not on the call — and the comparison that makes it a signal requires pulling the prior quarter's 10-Q and diffing the tax paragraph. If it were priced there would be at least one sell-side or newswire note framing the Q3 print as a possible valuation-allowance quarter, and with only two analysts covering the name there is none; the consensus is a single clean $0.18 with no reconciliation between a GAAP and an ex-tax number, which is what you would not see if anyone had modelled a $0.40/share non-cash credit. The 'reasonably possible / future reporting period' construction is the standard ASC 740 pre-announcement companies file one to four quarters before they act, and Q3 (ended 31 July 2026) would be the fifth consecutive profitable quarter.
findings.independence: None that is genuinely independent — the finding IS the diff between two of the company's own filings, the Q1 10-Q at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/740664/000143774926008410/rfil20260131_10q.htm (allowance $4,538,000, no release language, negative evidence still stated in the present tense). The 11,424,572 diluted share count used for the per-share arithmetic is from the Q2 8-K earnings exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/740664/000143774926020657/ex_975747.htm, filed the same day, so treat all three as one source cluster. Weight of timing risk is real: the fiscal-year-end (31 October) assessment is the more conventional moment to act, so the low end of my band is a Q3 that merely repeats the language.

findings.finding: The -52% slide from the 16 July 2026 peak of $21.50 to $10.27 has no disclosed company-specific cause: EDGAR's full filing history for CIK 0000740664 shows the last 8-K of any kind was 2026-06-15, with nothing since except an ARS/DEF 14A on 2026-07-28, a routine 13G on 2026-07-29 and a 13G/A on 2026-08-14 — no S-3, no shelf takedown, no 424B, no prospectus supplement, and Form 4 activity only in the company's own recurring quarterly cluster (13 Jan, 14 Apr, 14 Jul).
findings.source_date: 2026-09-11 (accessed; most recent filing listed 2026-08-14, most recent 8-K 2026-06-15)
findings.why_not_priced: The sweep's own brief treats the -22.5% 20-day drawdown as the single most specific question on this name, which is how most participants will read it too: a halving into a confirmed date reads as the market discounting a bad quarter or an imminent raise. The filing record says the opposite — a $110m company that had actually lost a customer, drawn on a shelf, or seen management sell would normally leave a trace on EDGAR, and there is none. If the market were pricing a dilution risk you would expect at least an active S-3 takedown or a borrow build; if it were pricing a fundamental break you would expect an 8-K or a withdrawn guide. What is left is the unwind of a narrative re-rating (Russell 3000 inclusion 29 June, Zacks #1 on 23 July) rather than new information, which makes the reaction function into the print more symmetric than the drawdown implies.
findings.independence: Company IR press-release page https://rfindustries.com/investor-overview/press-releases/ carries nothing between the Russell 3000 inclusion and the 31 August earnings-date notice — a separate channel from EDGAR, same conclusion. I could NOT verify a 2026 short-interest figure (the numbers returned by search resolved to 2025-dated MarketBeat URLs and were discarded), so no borrow-side corroboration is claimed.

findings.finding: COMEX copper ran at or near all-time highs through the whole of RF Industries' fiscal Q3 (1 May - 31 July 2026), printing a record $6.83/lb in August and sitting at $6.47/lb on 11 September, +41.2% over twelve months — against a business where custom cabling (37% of H1 FY2026 sales) plus interconnect (35%) is 72% of revenue and where the bar management set is a record 35.1% gross margin it called sustainable above $20m of quarterly revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Two analysts cover this name and the margin line they are modelling is the 35.1% management guided to as sustainable; nobody builds a copper pass-through lag into a $110m connector assembler. If input cost were in the price you would see a sell-side margin cut or at least a preview flagging it, and the only rating action in the window was a generic Zacks strong-buy-to-hold on 22 August. The mechanism is small but one-directional: RFIL buys finished cable, so a rising copper input shows up with a one-to-two-quarter lag precisely in the quarter being reported, and at roughly 15-25% of cabling COGS a 10% input move is worth about a point of gross margin, or ~$0.02 of EPS against a $0.18 bar.
findings.independence: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/14/copper-trump-tariffs-metal-commodities-trade-war.html (URL path confirms 2026-08-14) independently documents the record COMEX level and the Section 232 tariff overhang. Honest caveat: Q2 FY2026 (Feb-Apr) already carried copper near records and still printed 35.1%, so the quarter-over-quarter delta is not something I could establish, which is why the band is wide and the point estimate small.

baseline_tension: My net tilt is mildly positive and therefore cuts against the -22.49% 20-day run-up, but not against the skew — the baseline's 25-delta skew is null, so the market makes no directional statement here at all — and the run-up itself is the thing I am disputing, since EDGAR shows nothing that would justify reading it as information rather than as the unwind of a June-July index-add and momentum bid.
